title: 第339章 那一年第338章 男孩与女孩
content_zh:
“洛一？”
她笑起来，眼睛弯成了两道浅浅的月牙：“真好听。”
男孩怔怔地望着她，瞳孔中倒影着她巧笑嫣然的模样……
从那天起，弗嘉丽开始偷偷给洛一送饭。
起初她还有些紧张，每次都像做贼一样东张西望，绕着村子里的矮墙和柴垛摸到教堂后面那间废弃的小屋。
她把用旧布包好的面包或者烤饼放在石阶下面，然后躲到不远处的橡树后面，等洛一出来拿走，她才悄悄离开。
后来她渐渐习惯了这件事，胆子也越来越大。
她不再躲在树后面，而是直接把吃的塞进洛一手里，然后坐在旁边的石头上，托着腮看他吃完。
夏天的傍晚总是很长，蝉鸣在田野里此起彼伏，像是一首没有结尾的歌。
洛一坐在石阶上小口小口地吃着面包，弗嘉丽坐在旁边晃着腿，有一搭没一搭地说话。
“今天爸爸带回来一只受伤的野兔，我偷偷藏了点给你。”
“学校里的老师又说我写字好看了。”
弗嘉丽有时候说着说着就停了，歪着头看他，半真半假地抱怨：“你怎么总不说话呀，跟个闷葫芦似的。”
洛一咽下嘴里的食物，认真想了想，然后小声说：“我在听的。”
弗嘉丽愣了一下，然后“噗”地笑了出来：“知道啦知道啦，那你继续听吧，我继续讲。”
——那是一个夏末的午后。
村东头那条小河在阳光下泛着粼粼的光，几个孩子在河边打闹嬉戏。
弗嘉丽蹲在岸边，伸手拨弄着清凉的河水，忽然脚下一滑，整个人失去平衡，扑通一声栽进了水里。
河水并不算深，但对于一个七八岁的女孩来说，足以将她整个人淹没。
她慌乱地扑腾着，水花四溅，却怎么也找不到可以借力的地方。

岸边的几个孩子吓得尖叫着四散奔逃，有人喊着“弗嘉丽掉水里了”，却没有人敢下水去救她，只有一个瘦小的身影冲了过来。
洛一毫不犹豫地跳进了河里。
他的水性算不上多好，但他拼命游到弗嘉丽身边，用尽全身的力气托住她的腰，把她往岸边推。
弗嘉丽呛了好几口水，本能地紧紧抓住他的手臂，洛一咬着牙，脚踩着河底的淤泥，一步一步把她推上了岸。
等弗嘉丽趴在岸边剧烈地咳嗽起来时，她才意识到，身后那个推她上来的人，没有跟着上来。
她回过头，看见河面上只剩几圈正在扩散的涟漪，洛一的身影已经消失在了浑浊的水面之下。
弗嘉丽哭喊着跑去找人，带着几个大人回来的时候，洛一已经被河水冲到了下游的一个浅滩处，半截身子搁在沙地上，脸色苍白得吓人。
大人们把他捞上来，按压胸口，折腾了好一阵，他才猛地咳出一大口水，悠悠转醒。
他看到弗嘉丽红肿的眼睛，还没来得及说话，就被她扑上来抱住了，哭得喘不上气。
“你这个笨蛋——！”
洛一康复之后的某天清晨，弗嘉丽兴冲冲地跑到教堂后面那间破屋时，脸上的表情比以往任何一次都要明亮。
她一把推开门，拉着他粗糙的袖口就往外面拽：“洛一！跟我来！”
洛一被她拽得踉跄了一下，茫然地问：“去……去哪？”
“回家呀！”弗嘉丽回过头，浅金色的眼眸亮得像被阳光点亮的溪水：“爸爸妈妈说，要收养你！以后你就有家啦！”
洛一整个人仿佛被那道光芒击中了，他张了张嘴，什么话也没能说出来，只是呆呆地看着弗嘉丽。
弗嘉丽拉着他快步穿过田间小径，绕过几棵老橡树，来到了村子口那栋带着矮篱笆院子的木屋前。
她推开院门，拉着洛一就要往屋里走，但洛一却忽然停住了脚步。
他站在门槛前，低头看着自己那双沾着泥、指甲缝里还有灰的赤脚，又看了看面前那扇敞开的木门，门内铺着干净的地板，阳光从窗户照进来，将地板映得亮堂堂的。
他踌蹰着停了下来。
弗嘉丽的父母从屋里走出来。父亲是个面容温和的中年人，母亲系着围裙，笑容和蔼。

他们看到门口那个瘦小的男孩，目光里没有嫌弃，只有怜惜。
content_en:
"Luo Yi?"
She smiled, her eyes curved into two shallow crescent moons: "It sounds so good."
The boy stared at her blankly, her smiling face reflected in his pupils...
From that day on, Fu Jiali began to secretly deliver meals to Luo Yi.
She was a little nervous at first, and every time she looked around like a thief, walking around the low walls and firewood piles in the village to find the abandoned hut behind the church.
She put the bread or scones wrapped in old cloth under the stone steps, then hid behind an oak tree not far away, and waited for Luo Yi to come out and take it away before she quietly left.
Later, she gradually got used to it and became more and more courageous.
She no longer hid behind the tree, but directly put the food into Luo Yi's hand, then sat on the stone next to her, holding her chin and watching him finish.
Summer evenings are always very long, and the cicadas chirp one after another in the fields, like a song without an end.
Luo Yi sat on the stone steps and ate bread in small bites. Fujiali sat next to him, swinging his legs and talking intermittently.
"Dad brought back an injured hare today, and I secretly hid some for you."
"The teacher at school also said that my handwriting is good."
Fu Jiali sometimes stopped talking, tilted her head to look at him, and complained half-seriously: "Why don't you always talk? You're like a boring gourd."
Luo Yi swallowed the food in his mouth, thought about it seriously, and then whispered, "I'm listening."
Fu Jiali was stunned for a moment, and then burst out laughing: "I know, I know, then you continue to listen, and I will continue to talk."
——It was a late summer afternoon.
The small river at the east end of the village was sparkling in the sun, and several children were playing and playing by the river.
Fu Jiali squatted on the bank, reaching out to fiddle with the cool river water. Suddenly her foot slipped, she lost her balance, and fell into the water with a splash.
The river was not very deep, but for a seven or eight-year-old girl, it was enough to submerge her whole body.
She was thrashing around in panic, water splashing everywhere, but she couldn't find any place to use her strength.
Several children on the shore were so frightened that they screamed and ran away. Someone shouted, "Fujiali has fallen into the water," but no one dared to go into the water to save her. Only a thin figure rushed over.
Luo Yi jumped into the river without hesitation.
His water skills were not very good, but he swam desperately to Fujiali, used all his strength to hold her waist, and pushed her to the shore.
Fu Jiali choked several times and instinctively grabbed his arm tightly. Luo Yi gritted his teeth, stepped on the mud at the bottom of the river, and pushed her to the shore step by step.
When Fu Jiali lay on the shore and coughed violently, she realized that the person behind her who pushed her up did not follow her.
She turned back and saw only a few spreading ripples on the river, and Luo Yi's figure had disappeared under the turbid water.
Fu Jiali cried and ran to find someone. When she came back with a few adults, Luo Yi had been washed to a shallow place downstream by the river. Half of his body was resting on the sand, his face was frighteningly pale.
The adults picked him up and pressed his chest. After struggling for a while, he suddenly coughed up a large amount of water and woke up leisurely.
He saw Fujiali's red and swollen eyes, and before he could speak, she rushed forward and hugged him, crying so hard that he couldn't breathe.
"You idiot-!"
One morning after Luo Yi recovered, when Fujiali ran excitedly to the shabby room behind the church, the expression on her face was brighter than ever before.
She pushed open the door and pulled his rough cuffs out: "Luo Yi! Follow me!"
Luo Yi staggered when she pulled her, and asked in a daze: "Where...where are you going?"
"Go home!" Fu Jiali turned around, her light golden eyes as bright as the stream lit by the sun: "Mom and dad said they want to adopt you! You will have a home in the future!"
Luo's whole body seemed to be hit by that light. He opened his mouth,He couldn't say anything, he just stared at Fujiali blankly.
Fujiali pulled him quickly through the field paths, bypassing several old oak trees, and came to the wooden house with a low fenced yard at the entrance of the village.
She pushed open the courtyard door and pulled Luo Yi towards the house, but Luo Yi suddenly stopped.
He stood in front of the threshold, looking down at his bare feet, which were stained with mud and still had dust between his nails, and then looked at the open wooden door in front of him. There was a clean floor inside the door, and the sun shone in through the window, making the floor bright.
He hesitated and stopped.
Fujiali's parents came out of the house. My father is a middle-aged man with a gentle face, and my mother wears an apron and has a kind smile.
When they saw the thin boy at the door, there was no disgust in their eyes, only pity.
